name: Pricing X4.1 — Modifier 22 Clinical Coding Review (CCCR)
description: Walk the Pricing SOP for a claim billed with modifier 22. Open the Event Resolution tab and identify the active PX_X4 hard edit to resolve. Confirm the claim was not already reviewed by the Provider Edits Team (Notes carry no Editing/Bundling/CCCR keyword), confirm medical records are on the claim (Attachments document number present), route the claim for a Clinical Claim & Coding Review (CCCR), read the returned recommendation to process at 120% of the allowance, raise the allowance to 120% on the Search → Pricing CX% (100 → 120) and on the Manual Pricing Allowed amount (80 → 96), then pay the claim.

steps.name: Identify the PX_X4 hard edit on Event Resolution
steps.description: Navigate to the Event Resolution tab and review all edits set on the claim. The active PX_X4 edit — Pricing, modifier 22 additional payment review — is shown as a hard edit and is highlighted in red. This is the event you need to resolve.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab and reviews the edits list, where the active PX_X4 hard edit is shown.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' and review every edit. The active PX_X4 edit (modifier 22 additional payment review) is a hard edit, highlighted in red — this is the event to resolve.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the PX_X4 hard edit on Event Resolution

steps.name: Check for prior Provider Edits review
steps.description: Open the Notes tab and review the comments currently available, looking for words such as Editing, Bundling, or CCCR. If the claim has already been reviewed by the Provider Edits Team, process it per the team's recommendations; if it has not been reviewed, proceed. In this scenario, the comments contain none of those keywords, so the claim has not been reviewed by the Provider Edits Team and the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Notes tab and reviews the comments, which contain no Editing/Bundling/CCCR keyword.
steps.hint: Open 'Notes' and read the comments. None contain Editing, Bundling, or CCCR, so the claim was not previously reviewed by the Provider Edits Team — proceed.
steps.checklistItem: Check for prior Provider Edits review

steps.name: Check for medical records on the claim
steps.description: Determine whether medical records are available on the claim. Open the Attachments sub-tab of the Attachments tab and check whether a document number is present in the Attachments section, which displays a Type label and a Document number. In this scenario a Document number (25035878888) is present with a Type of Medical Records, so medical records are available and the claim must be routed to the Provider Edits Team for a Clinical Claim and Coding Review (CCCR).
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Attachments sub-tab and reads the Document number (25035878888) and Type (Medical Records).
steps.hint: Open 'Attachment' → 'Attachments'. A Document number (25035878888) is present with Type Medical Records, so medical records are available — route the claim for a Clinical Coding Review.
steps.checklistItem: Check for medical records on the claim

steps.name: Submit the Clinical Coding Review request
steps.description: Route the claim to the Provider Edits Team. Open the Action menu (top-right) and select Clinical Coding Review under the Request claim review group — the Request claim review — Clinical Coding Review dialog opens. Verify the records are added to the request and that the Attachment Number (DCN) field carries the document number identified in the Attachments step (25035878888). In the Comments box, the request reads "Please review coding as modifier 22 billed with medical records received." Click Submit to send the request.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Action menu → Request claim review → Clinical Coding Review dialog and clicks Submit, dispatching the submit_ccr action (which writes the Provider-Edits 120% recommendation into the Notes tab).
steps.hint: Open the Action menu (top-right), select Clinical Coding Review under Request claim review, confirm the Attachment Number (DCN) and comments, then click Submit.
steps.checklistItem: Submit the Clinical Coding Review request

steps.name: Read the Provider Edits recommendation
steps.description: Once the claim returns from the Provider Edits review, open the Notes tab and review the new recommendation. The recommendation will be one of two options: process at 100% of the allowance (no additional payment for modifier 22) or process at 120% of the allowance (an additional 20% on top of the existing allowance). In this scenario, the recommendation is to process at 120%, so the trainee proceeds to identify and apply the correct 120% allowance.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee returns to the Notes tab and reads the Provider-Edits recommendation written back by the submit_ccr action.
steps.hint: Return to 'Notes'. The Provider Edits recommendation now reads process at 120% of the allowance — proceed to apply the 120% allowance.

steps.name: Get pricing and update CX% to 120
steps.description: Navigate to the Search tab, then the Pricing sub-tab, and scroll to the Claim Lines section. Review the displayed claim line and select Get Pricing at the bottom of the section. The system will calculate and display the 100% allowance, and the CX% field for Line 1 will display 100. Calculate the 120% recommendation by multiplying the 100% allowance by 1.2. To reflect the recommended pricing, manually update the CX% value for Line 1 from 100 to 120.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Get Pricing and edits the Line 1 CX% field from 100 to 120.
steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Pricing', click Get Pricing (CX% shows 100), then change the Line 1 CX% to 120.
steps.checklistItem: Get pricing and update CX% to 120

steps.name: Update the Manual Pricing Allowed amount to 96
steps.description: Navigate to the Claim Data tab, then the Pricing sub-tab, and open the Manual Pricing (MP) pop-up. The table shows columns No., Service, Billed, Allowed, Reason amount, Units, Reason, Price reason code, and QPA amount, with the first row reading 1, PHT, 55.00, 80, —, 1, —, 3C, 0.00. Click the pencil/edit icon and change the Line 1 Allowed amount from 80 to 96 (80 × 1.2 = 96) to reflect the 120% allowance, then proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Manual Pricing pop-up and edits the Line 1 Allowed amount from 80 to 96.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Pricing', open the Manual Pricing pop-up, and change the Line 1 Allowed amount from 80 to 96 (80 × 1.2).
steps.checklistItem: Update the Manual Pricing Allowed amount to 96

steps.name: Submit Pay decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Pay' from the dropdown menu and click Submit. With the allowance raised to 120% on both the Search → Pricing CX% and the Manual Pricing Allowed amount, the claim is paid with the additional 20% allowed for modifier 22.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Pay decision in the submit dialog.
steps.hint: Pick 'Pay' from the Decision dropdown in the claim header, then click Submit and confirm in the dialog.

stepSummaryForResults.name: PX_X4 hard edit identified on Event Resolution
Prior Provider Edits review checked (no CCCR keyword)
Medical records confirmed on the claim
Get Pricing run and CX% updated to 120
